statement: Define reverse(n) for a positive integer n as follows: if n has decimal digits d_0,...,d_{k-1} with n = sum_{j=0}^{k-1} d_j * 10^j, d_{k-1} != 0, and 0 <= d_j <= 9, then reverse(n) = sum_{j=0}^{k-1} d_j * 10^{k-1-j} (the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits and ignoring leading zeros). The function returns a result r, and r is the cardinality of the set S = { x | (there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i]) or (there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = reverse(nums[i])) }. Equivalently, r is the number of distinct integers in the array formed by appending reverse(nums[0]), reverse(nums[1]), ..., reverse(nums[len(nums)-1]) to nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, count_distinct_integers returns a result r; in particular, it does not fail, overflow, or panic.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i] }|, the number of distinct values occurring in nums.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = reverse(nums[i]) }|, where reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i] }| + |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = reverse(nums[i]) }|, where reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums) such that reverse(nums[i]) = nums[j], then r = |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i] }|, where reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every i,j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums) we have reverse(nums[i]) != nums[j], then r = |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i] }| + |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = reverse(nums[i]) }|, where reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists an integer v such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = v, then r = 1 if reverse(v) = v, and r = 2 if reverse(v) != v, where reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the 2*len(nums) integers nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1], reverse(nums[0]), ..., reverse(nums[len(nums)-1]) are pairwise distinct, then r = 2 * len(nums), where reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r for nums, and nums' is any slice that is a permutation of nums (that is, len(nums') = len(nums) and there is a bijection p from {0,...,len(nums)-1} to itself with nums'[i] = nums[p(i)] for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums)), then if the function returns r' on nums', r' = r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r for nums, and nums' is any slice satisfying the same constraints and containing every value that occurs in nums (i.e., for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) there exists j with 0 <= j < len(nums') and nums'[j] = nums[i]), then if the function returns r' on nums', r' >= r.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if every nums[i] is a power of ten (i.e., for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums) there exists k >= 0 with nums[i] = 10^k), then r = D if 1 occurs among the values nums[i], and r = D + 1 otherwise, where D = |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i] }|.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exist i,j with 0 <= i < len(nums) and 0 <= j < len(nums) such that nums[i] = reverse(nums[j]), then r <= D_orig + D_rev - 1, where D_orig = |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = nums[i] }| and D_rev = |{ x | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and x = reverse(nums[i]) }|, and reverse(n) is the integer obtained by reversing the decimal digits of n and dropping leading zeros.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1, len(nums) <= 100000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.
